_what: TRACK A -- THE RESERVOIR. CA_MULT is hard-coded 1.0 in qal/qal_hop_gates.py:79 ('IDENTICAL banks (a real chain): equal caps -> an LC half-cycle') and every hop measured in this campaign moved charge PEER TO PEER between equal banks. Nothing in the architecture requires that. This track feeds the receiving bank from a LARGE SHARED TANK instead, sweeps the tank size, and asks whether the depth fade stops and whether the level beats CMOS.

inherited_and_frozen_NOT_reopened.t_pred_rescale: sk.t_pred(L, ca) hard-codes C_ser = ca/2, which is the EQUAL-BANK series capacitance and is only correct at CA_MULT = 1. The ZCS instant itself is MEASURED by probe, never taken from t_pred.

ACCEPTANCE_pre_stated.A_FADE_STOPS: PASS iff, in the 6-bank RESERVOIR chain, the HIGH/LOW separation stays ABOVE 6.44 mV at depth >= 5 (i.e. banks 5 and 6 both clear it) AND keeps the correct sign at every depth. The committed peer chain fails this at depth 3 (1.52 mV) on magnitude and alternates sign from depth 2. Anything that clears 6.44 mV at depth 5 and 6 is a PASS; a separation that merely falls more slowly is a PARTIAL and will be labelled so.
ACCEPTANCE_pre_stated.B_LEVEL: PASS iff the MEASURED end-to-end level at the ALU's real 6.91 fF sink load, at some swept CA_MULT, is < 94.174 ps. The level is t_level_ps = max(t_hop, t_valid90) read off the waveform by the inherited extractor -- NEVER composed from a hop time plus a settle time taken from a different circuit. (A composed t_settle over-stated a bank settle by 1.29-1.84x once already in this campaign and swapped two objective surfaces.)
ACCEPTANCE_pre_stated.C_OVERSHOOT_RELIABILITY: The delivered rail and its peak must be reported against the 1.65 V characterisation limit. A point whose V(bank) peak exceeds 1.65 V is flagged OUT-OF-ENVELOPE and its level is reported but NOT credited.
ACCEPTANCE_pre_stated.D_TANK_HONESTY: Every row that does not carry a measured recharge cost is labelled a BOUND, not a result. An ideal-source tank row is a BOOKING and will be printed as one. This campaign has had three verdicts overturned by exactly that booking (the cells' gate burn, the ideal PWL gate drives, the park driver).

EXPECTATION_pre_stated_DERIVED_to_be_tes.E1_delivered_rail_RISES: DERIVED from lossless LC: a source C_A at dV into C_B through L rings C_B to 2*dV*m/(m+1) with m = C_A/C_B. The committed CA_MULT=1 real-load point peaks at VBPK = 1.0881874 V against a lossless ideal of dV = 1.65 V, i.e. a MEASURED loss factor r = VBPK/ideal = 0.6595. Holding r fixed predicts VBPK = 1.451 / 1.813 / 1.978 / 2.073 / 2.175 V at CA_MULT = 2 / 5 / 10 / 20 / ideal. I EXPECT r to FALL as the tank grows (more charge moved through the same 10 ohm + switch, and a harder drive into the settling gates), so I expect the measured peaks to come in BELOW those numbers. PASS/FAIL of this expectation is recorded either way.
EXPECTATION_pre_stated_DERIVED_to_be_tes.E2_OVERSHOOT_YES_I_EXPECT_IT: I DO expect overshoot above the tank voltage at large CA_MULT. The condition for V(bank)_peak > V(tank) is r > (m+1)/(2m), i.e. r > 0.55 at m=10 and r > 0.5 in the ideal-source limit. The MEASURED r at CA_MULT=1 is 0.6595, ABOVE both. So I pre-state: at CA_MULT >= 5 the bank rail peak EXCEEDS the tank voltage, and at dV = 1.65 V it will BREACH the 1.65 V characterisation limit -- probably reaching 1.8-2.2 V. That is a reliability finding, not a bonus. I pre-state the consequence: the useful reservoir operating point will have to be found by LOWERING dV, not by raising the tank, and I will sweep at least one lower-dV point if the limit is breached. NOTE the counter-case so it cannot be claimed after the fact: if r falls below 0.5 as m grows, no overshoot occurs and the rail asymptotes below the tank voltage.
EXPECTATION_pre_stated_DERIVED_to_be_tes.E3_VBEND_vs_VBPK: VBEND (the SETTLED rail, after the isolated bank charges its own 4 x 6.91 fF outputs) is 1.442x below VBPK at CA_MULT=1. That droop is a charge-sharing fact of the ISOLATED bank and I expect it to survive the tank almost unchanged in RATIO, because the tank is disconnected at ZCS. So I expect the delivered SETTLED rail to rise roughly in proportion to the peak, not to be held flat. A tank that is HELD CONNECTED through settling would remove the droop entirely; that is a DIFFERENT architecture and I will run it as a separately labelled row, not fold it into the sweep.
EXPECTATION_pre_stated_DERIVED_to_be_tes.E4_LEVEL_BEATS_CMOS_but_the_hop_GROWS: The brief's composed prediction (~40 ps settle at a 1.2 V rail + the 34.29 ps MEASURED hop = ~74 ps) contains an error I pre-state before measuring: t_hop = pi*sqrt(L*C_ser) and C_ser goes from C_B/2 at CA_MULT=1 to C_B in the tank limit, so the HOP GROWS BY sqrt(2) = 1.414x, from 34.29 ps to ~48.5 ps at fixed L = 4 nH. I therefore predict the level at CA_MULT=20, L=4 nH lands near 48 + 35 = ~83 ps, NOT 74 ps -- still a PASS on acceptance B but by a smaller margin. I further predict that re-optimising L downward (L ~ 2 nH restores t_hop ~ 34 ps at the tank's C_ser) recovers the rest, and I will sweep L at the best CA_MULT to test it.
EXPECTATION_pre_stated_DERIVED_to_be_tes.E5_THE_RESERVOIR_SPENDS_THE_RECYCLING__m: This is the expectation I most expect to be told off for if I get it wrong, so it goes first in the energy section. In the PEER chain, bank N's charge BECOMES bank N+1's charge -- the recycling IS the peer hop, and that is what makes the loss adiabatic. A tank-fed bank does NOT consume its predecessor's charge; the predecessor's charge is left stranded on a rail that is then dumped. So I expect the tank architecture to BUY SPEED AND SPEND ENERGY unless the bank's charge is RETURNED to the tank on a second (reverse) half-cycle at the end of the beat. I pre-state the two rows I will measure for (e): (i) NO-RETURN: energy out of the tank per hop, with the bank's charge written off -- I expect this to be ~2x the bank's stored energy and therefore WORSE than CMOS (1/2)CV^2 per transition; (ii) WITH-RETURN: switch re-closed after the settle window, charge rung back into the tank, net tank energy per full cycle measured -- I expect this to be a few x smaller and to be the only honest reservoir row.
EXPECTATION_pre_stated_DERIVED_to_be_tes.E6_FADE: I expect the fade to STOP. Each bank becomes depth-1 in RAIL, and a CMOS inverter on a good rail restores its own output level, so the separation should stay in the hundreds of mV at every depth rather than collapsing 528 -> 0.001 mV. The residual risk I pre-state: the tank must supply 6 banks, so it droops; and 6 idle inductors hanging off one tank can divert charge (chain3 AMENDMENT A3 MEASURED 42.3% diverted into ONE idle inductor when the source-side cut was missing). I therefore use the source-side cut on EVERY hop including the reservoir hops, which is a DEVIATION from restore5 AMENDMENT A3 (which omits it on a reservoir hop because there was only one). The deviation is justified by A3's own measured reason and is recorded here in advance.
